e: And these are the laws
that you shall set before them.
If you buy a Hebrew slave [who is a son of a Hebrew],
he shall serve [you] for six years,
but in the seventh [year] he is to go out free, for naught [without liability].
If he came by himself [unmarried], he shall go out by himself.
If he was married,
his wife shall go out with him.
If his master should give him a wife,
and she bears him sons or daughters,
then the woman and her children belong to her master,
and he shall go out by himself.
If the slave explicitly says,
“I have come to love my master,
my wife and my children,
I do not want to go out free.”
His master must bring him to [before] the judges.
He must then bring him next to the door,
or to the doorpost,
and his master shall pierce his ear with an awl.
He then serves his master [will be a working servant for him,] forever.

t: וַאֲרֵי יְזַבֵּן גְבַר יָת בְּרַתֵּהּ לְאַמְהוּ
e: If a man sells his daughter to be a maidservant,
she shall not go out [free] in the manner of male slaves.

h: אִם־רָעָ֞ה בְּעֵינֵ֧י אֲדֹנֶ֛יהָ אֲשֶׁר־לא [ל֥וֹ] יְעָדָ֖הּ וְהֶפְדָּ֑הּ
t: אִם בִּישָׁא בְּעֵינֵי רִבּוֹנַהּ דִיקַיְמַהּ לֵהּ וְיִפְרְקִנַהּ
לִגְבַר אָחֳרָן לֵית לֵהּ רְשׁוּ לְזַבּוֹנַהּ בְּמִשְׁלְטֵהּ בַהּ:
e: If she is displeasing to her master, who had not designated [for otherwise he would have designated] her as his wife, he must allow her to be redeemed.
He has no power [right] to sell her to an alien people [another man] for he has dealt deceitfully with [controlled] her.
If he has designated her as a wife for his son,
he must grant her exactly the same rights as daughters [of Yisrael].
If he takes himself another [wife],
her sustenance, her clothing and her conjugal rights he must not diminish.

t: וְאִם תְּלָת אִלֵין לָא יַעְבֵּד לַהּ
e: If he does not do these three things to her,
she goes out free with no repayment of money.
If one strikes a man and he [the victim] dies, he shall be put to death.
But if he did not lie in wait [to ambush him]
but [from before] God [he was] brought it to his hand,
then I will designate for you a place,
to which he can flee [and find refuge].

t: וַאֲרֵי יַרְשַׁע גְבַר עַל חַבְרֵהּ לְמִקְטְלֵהּ בִנְכִילוּ
e: But if a man plots against his neighbor to kill him intentionally, you may [even] take him
from My altar
to put him to death.
Whoever strikes his father or his mother shall be put to death.

h: וְגֹנֵ֨ב אִ֧ישׁ וּמְכָר֛וֹ וְנִמְצָ֥א בְיָד֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃
t: וְדִיִגְנוּב נַפְשָׁא מִן בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וִיזַבְּנִנֵהּ וְיִשְׁתְּכַח בִּידֵהּ אִתְקְטָלָא יִתְקְטֵל:
e: Whoever steals [kidnaps] a man [person from B’nei Yisrael] and sells him, if he is found in his hand, he shall be put to death.
Whoever curses his father or his mother shall be put to death.
When men quarrel
and one man hits his fellow
with a stone or with [his] fist;
and he [the victim] does not die but becomes bedridden [falls to idleness],

h: אִם־יָק֞וּם וְהִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בַּח֛וּץ עַל־מִשְׁעַנְתּ֖וֹ וְנִקָּ֣ה הַמַּכֶּ֑ה
t: אִם יְקוּם וִיהַלִיךְ בְּבָרָא עַל בּוּרְיֵהּ וִיהֵי זַכָּאָה מָחְיָא
e: If he gets up and is able to walk on the outside on his own power, the one who struck him shall be acquitted.
Still he must pay for his loss of work, and must pay for his complete cure [the doctor’s fee].

h: וְכִֽי־יַכֶּה֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶת־עַבְדּ֜וֹ א֤וֹ אֶת־אֲמָתוֹ֙ בַּשֵּׁ֔בֶט
t: וַאֲרֵי יִמְחֵי גְבַר יָת עַבְדֵהּ אוֹ יָת אַמְתֵהּ בְּשָׁלְטָן
e: If a man strikes his male or female slave with a rod [power],
and [the slave] dies under his hand,
[the death] must be avenged [judged].

t: בְּרַם אִם יוֹמָא אוֹ תְרֵין יוֹמִין יִתְקַיָם
e: However if he [the slave] survives for a day or two,
[his death] is not avenged [judged],
for he [the slave] is his [master’s] property.

h: וְכִֽי־יִנָּצ֣וּ אֲנָשִׁ֗ים וְנָ֨גְפ֜וּ אִשָּׁ֤ה הָרָה֙ וְיָצְא֣וּ יְלָדֶ֔יהָ
עָנ֣וֹשׁ יֵעָנֵ֗שׁ כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָשִׁ֤ית עָלָיו֙ בַּ֣עַל הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה
t: וַאֲרֵי יִנְצוּן גֻבְרִין וְיִמְחוּן אִתְּתָא מַעַדְיָא וְיִפְּקוּן וַלְדָהָא
אִתְגְבָאָה יִתְגְבֵי כְּמָא דִי יְשַׁוִי עֲלוֹהִי בַּעֲלַהּ דְאִתְּתָא
e: If men will fight and they strike a pregnant woman, causing her to miscarry,
but there is no fatal injury [to the woman],
he [the guilty one] is to be punished with a [monetary] penalty when the husband demands compensation.
He shall pay as determined by the judges.
However if there is a fatal injury,
you shall give [up] a life for a life.
[Compensation of] an eye for an eye,
[of] a tooth for a tooth,
[of] a hand for a hand,
[of] a foot for a foot.
[Compensation of] a burn for a burn,
[of] a wound for a wound,
[of] a bruise [beating] for a bruise [beating].

h: וְכִֽי־יַכֶּ֨ה אִ֜ישׁ אֶת־עֵ֥ין עַבְדּ֛וֹ אֽוֹ־אֶת־עֵ֥ין אֲמָת֖וֹ וְשִֽׁחֲתָ֑הּ
t: וַאֲרֵי יִמְחֵי גְבַר יָת עֵינָא דְעַבְדֵהּ אוֹ יָת עֵינָא דְאַמְתֵהּ וִיחַבְּלִנַהּ לְבַר
e: If a man strikes the eye of his slave, or the eye of his female slave, and destroys [blinds] it,
he shall set him [the slave] free as compensation for the eye.

t: וְאִם שִׁנָא דְעַבְדֵהּ אוֹ שִׁנָא דְאַמְתֵהּ יַפֵּל לְבַר
e: If [he knocks out] the tooth of his slave, or knocks out the tooth of his female slave,
he shall set him [the slave] free as compensation for the tooth.

h: וְכִֽי־יִגַּ֨ח שׁ֥וֹר אֶת־אִ֛ישׁ א֥וֹ אֶת־אִשָּׁ֖ה וָמֵ֑ת
סָק֨וֹל יִסָּקֵ֜ל הַשּׁ֗וֹר וְלֹ֤א יֵאָכֵל֙ אֶת־בְּשָׂר֔וֹ
t: וַאֲרֵי יַגַח תּוֹרָא יָת גַבְרָא אוֹ יָת אִתְּתָא וִימוּת
אִתְרְגָמָא יִתְרְגֵם תּוֹרָא וְלָא יִתְאָכֵל יָת בִּסְרֵהּ
e: If an ox gores a man or woman and the victim dies, the ox shall be stoned [to death],
and its flesh may not be eaten.
The owner of the ox shall go unpunished.

h: וְאִ֡ם שׁוֹר֩ נַגָּ֨ח ה֜וּא מִתְּמֹ֣ל שִׁלְשֹׁ֗ם וְהוּעַ֤ד בִּבְעָלָיו֙ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁמְרֶ֔נּוּ
t: וְאִם תּוֹר נַגַח הוּא מֵאִתְּמַלֵי וּמִדְקַמוֹהִי וְיִתַּסְהֵד בְּמָרֵהּ וְלָא נַטְרֵהּ
e: But if the ox had gored yesterday and the day before, and a warning was given to its owner, but he had not taken proper precautions to guard it,
and kills a man or a woman,
the ox must be stoned,
and the owner also shall die [by Divine decree].
When an atonement fine shall be imposed on him,
he must give for the redemption of his soul
whatever sum is imposed on him.

t: אוֹ לְבַר יִשְׂרָאֵל יַגַח תּוֹרָא אוֹ לְבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל יַגָח
e: Whether it is a son [a minor lad] [of Yisrael] that is gored [by the ox] or a daughter [a minor girl] [of Yisrael] that it gored,
this law shall apply to it.

t: אִם לְעַבְדָא יַגַח תּוֹרָא אוֹ לְאַמְתָא
e: If the ox gored a male or female slave,
he must give thirty silver shekalim [selaim] to their master,
and the ox must be stoned.

h: וְכִֽי־יִפְתַּ֨ח אִ֜ישׁ בּ֗וֹר א֠וֹ כִּֽי־יִכְרֶ֥ה אִ֛ישׁ בֹּ֖ר וְלֹ֣א יְכַסֶּ֑נּוּ
t: וַאֲרֵי יִפְתַּח גְבַר גוֹב אוֹ אֲרֵי יִכְרֶה גְבַר גוֹב וְלָא יְכַסִנֵהּ
e: If a man uncovers a pit, or if a man digs a pit, and does not cover it,
and an ox or a donkey falls into it;
The owner of the pit must pay.
He must compensate its owner with money,
and the dead [animal] remains his [its original owner’s] possesion.

t: וַאֲרֵי יִגוֹף תּוֹר דִגְבַר יָת תּוֹרָא דְחַבְרֵהּ וִימוּת
וִיזַבְּנוּן יָת תּוֹרָא חַיָא וִיפַלְגוּן יָת כַּסְפֵּהּ
e: If a man’s ox injures his neighbor’s ox and it dies,
they shall sell the live ox and divide the money received for it.
They shall also divide [the value of] the dead animal.

h: א֣וֹ נוֹדַ֗ע כִּ֠י שׁ֣וֹר נַגָּ֥ח הוּא֙ מִתְּמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשֹׁ֔ם
t: אוֹ אִתְיְדַע אֲרֵי תוֹר נַגַח הוּא מֵאִתְּמַלֵי וּמִדְקַמוֹהִי
e: If it was known that it was a goring ox from yesterday and the day before,
but he had not taken proper precaution to guard it,
then he must pay full compensation, an ox for an ox.
The dead [animal] remains in the possession [of its owner].

t: אֲרֵי יִגְנוּב גְבַר תּוֹר אוֹ אִמָר
e: If a man steals an ox or a sheep,
and then slaughters or sells it,
he must pay five oxen for each ox,
and four sheep for each sheep.

t: אִם בְּמַחְתַּרְתָּא יִשְׁתְּכַח גַנָבָא וְיִתְמְחֵי וִימוּת
e: If the thief is found [caught] while breaking in, and is struck and killed,
there is no liability for his blood.

t: אִם עֵינָא דְסָהֲדַיָא נְפָלַת עֲלוֹהִי דְמָא לֵהּ
e: If the sun shone on him [eyes of witnesses fell upon him], there is liability for his blood.
He must make full restitution.
If he does not have [the means to do so],
he shall be sold [as a slave to pay] for his theft.

h: אִֽם־הִמָּצֵא֩ תִמָּצֵ֨א בְיָד֜וֹ הַגְּנֵבָ֗ה מִשּׁ֧וֹר עַד־חֲמ֛וֹר עַד־שֶׂ֖ה חַיִּ֑ים
t: אִם אִשְׁתְּכָחָא יִשְׁתְּכַח בִּידֵהּ גְנֻבְתָּא מִתּוֹר עַד חֲמַר עַד אִמַר כַּד אִנוּן חַיִין
e: If the stolen article is found in his hand [possession], whether it is an ox, donkey or sheep [that is alive],
he must pay two live animals.

t: אֲרֵי יֹאכִיל גְבַר חֲקַל אוֹ כְרָם
e: If he damages a field or vineyard with his animal —
he lets his livestock loose,
and [or] it feeds in another’s field —
from his [own] prime field and prime vineyard he must compensate [the owner].

h: כִּֽי־תֵצֵ֨א אֵ֜שׁ וּמָצְאָ֤ה קֹצִים֙ וְנֶאֱכַ֣ל גָּדִ֔ישׁ
t: אֲרֵי תִתַּפַּק נוּר וְיַשְׁכַּח כּוּבִין וְיֵיכוּל גְדִישִׁין
e: If a fire goes out of control and finds [catches on] thorns, and then consumes bound
or standing grain or a field,
full restitution must be made
by the one who started the fire.

h: כִּֽי־יִתֵּן֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֜הוּ כֶּ֤סֶף אֽוֹ־כֵלִים֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔ר
t: אֲרֵי יִתֵּן גְבַר לְחַבְרֵהּ כְּסַף אוֹ מָנִין לְמִטַר
אִם יִשְׁתְּכַח גַנָבָא יְשַׁלֵם עַל חַד תְּרֵין:
e: If a man gives his neighbor money or articles to safeguard
and they are stolen from the house of the [watch]man,
if the thief is found, he must pay double.

t: אִם לָא אוֹשִׁיט יְדֵהּ בְּמָא דִמְסַר לֵהּ חַבְרֵהּ:
e: If the thief is not found,
the owner of the house [the watchman] must come before the judges [Beis Din],
[to swear] that he did not lay a hand on his neighbor’s possessions [for his personal use] [that which his neighbor handed over to him].

h: עַֽל־כָּל־דְּבַר־פֶּ֡שַׁע עַל־שׁ֡וֹר עַל־חֲ֠מוֹר עַל־שֶׂ֨ה עַל־שַׂלְמָ֜ה עַל־כָּל־אֲבֵדָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֹאמַר֙ כִּי־ה֣וּא זֶ֔ה
t: עַל כָּל פִּתְגַם דְחוֹב עַל תּוֹר עַל חֲמַר עַל אִמָר עַל כְּסוּ עַל כָּל אֲבֶדְתָּא דִי יֵימַר אֲרֵי הוּא דֵין
e: In every question of dishonesty whether it involves an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or anything that was [allegedly] lost of which [a witness] says, “This is it!”
the claims of both parties must be brought to [before] the judges.
The one whom the judges find guilty,
must pay double restitution to his neighbor.

h: כִּֽי־יִתֵּן֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֜הוּ חֲמ֨וֹר אוֹ־שׁ֥וֹר אוֹ־שֶׂ֛ה וְכָל־בְּהֵמָ֖ה לִשְׁמֹ֑ר
t: אֲרֵי יִתֵּן גְבַר לְחַבְרֵהּ חֲמַר אוֹ תוֹר אוֹ אִמָר וְכָל בְּעִירָא לְמִטָר
וּמִית אוֹ אִתְּבַר אוֹ אִשְׁתְּבִי לֵית דְחָזֵי:
e: If a man gives his neighbor, a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any animal for safeguarding;
and it dies, or is injured, or is captured, and there is no eyewitness,

t: אִם לָא אוֹשִׁיט יְדֵהּ בְּמָא דִמְסַר לֵהּ חַבְרֵהּ
וִיקַבֵּל מָרֵהּ מִנֵהּ מוֹמָתָא וְלָא יְשַׁלֵם:
e: an oath to Adonoy shall be between them,
that he [the watcher] did not lay his hand on his neighbor’s possession [for his personal use] [that which his neighbor handed over to him].
The owner must accept it [the oath], and [the watcher] need not make restitution.
But if it was indeed stolen from him,
he must make restitution to its owner.
If it was torn apart [killed by wild beasts], he [the watcher] must provide witnesses [that is was torn apart].
He then need not pay for that which was torn apart.

h: וְכִֽי־יִשְׁאַ֥ל אִ֛ישׁ מֵעִ֥ם רֵעֵ֖הוּ וְנִשְׁבַּ֣ר אוֹ־מֵ֑ת
t: וַאֲרֵי יִשְׁאַל גְבַר מִן חַבְרֵהּ וְיִתְּבַר אוֹ מִית
e: If a man borrows something from his neighbor, and it becomes broken or dies;
if the owner is not [involved] with him, he [the borrower] must make full restitution.
If the owner is [involved] with him, then he [the borrower] need not make restitution.
If it was hired,
it [the ox] comes in its rental price.

h: וְכִֽי־יְפַתֶּ֣ה אִ֗ישׁ בְּתוּלָ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־אֹרָ֖שָׂה וְשָׁכַ֣ב עִמָּ֑הּ
t: וַאֲרֵי יְשַׁדֵל גְבַר בְתֻלְתָּא דִּי לָא מְאַרְסָא וְיִשְׁכּוּב עִמַהּ
e: If a man seduces a virgin who is not betrothed, and lies with her;
he must give the dowry to acquire [establish] her as his wife.

t: אִם מִצְבָּא לָא יִצְבֵּי אֲבוּהָא לְמִתְּנַהּ לֵהּ
e: If her father utterly refuses to give her to him,
he must give [the father] the weight of silver
equal to the dowry usually given to virgins.
You shall not allow a witch to live.

t: כָּל דְיִשְׁכּוּב עִם בְּעִירָא אִתְקְטָלָא יִתְקְטֵל:
e: Whoever lies with an animal must be put to death.
Whoever slaughters to a god [false gods of the peoples] must be condemned [to die].
[Sacrifices may be offered] to [the Name of] Adonoy alone.

t: וְגִיוֹרָא לָא תוֹנוּן וְלָא תְעִיקוּן לֵהּ
e: You must not abuse or oppress a stranger,
for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.
You must not mistreat any widow or orphan.
If you do mistreat him [them],
when he cries out to [before] Me,
I will indeed hear [obey] his cry.
Then I will cause My anger to flare,
and I will kill you by the sword.
Your wives will become widows
and your children will be orphans.

t: אִם כַּסְפָּא תּוֹזֵף בְּעַמִי לְעַנְיָא דִי עִמָךְ
e: When you lend money to My people, to the poor person who is with [among] you,
do not act toward him as a [demanding] creditor.
Do not place the burden of interest [an injury] upon him.
If you take your neighbor’s garment as security,
you must return it to him till sunset;
For this alone is his covering,
the garment [to cover] his skin.
With what shall he lie down [to sleep]?
If it happens that he cries out to [before] Me,
I will hear [obey] [his cry] for I am gracious.
Do not curse judges.
Do not curse a leader of your people.
[Your offering of] the fullness [of your newly ripened produce] and of your terumah-offering’s you must not delay.
The first-born of your sons, you shall give to [separate before] Me.
You must do likewise with your oxen and with your sheep.
Seven days it shall remain with its mother.
On the eighth day you must give it to [separate it before] Me.

t: וּבְשַׂר תְּלִישׁ מִן חֵיוָא חַיְתָא לָא תֵיכְלוּן
e: You shall be men of holiness to [before] Me,
and you must not eat flesh that was torn off in the field [from a living animal].
Throw it to the dog.

t: לָא תְשַׁוִי יְדָךְ עִם חַיָבָא לְמֶהֱוֵי לֵהּ
e: Do not accept a false report.
Do not join hands with a wicked man to be
a corrupt [false] witness [for him].

h: וְלֹא־תַעֲנֶ֣ה עַל־רִ֗ב לִנְטֹ֛ת אַחֲרֵ֥י רַבִּ֖ים לְהַטֹּֽת׃
t: וְלָא תִתְמְנַע מִלְאַלָפָא מָא דִבְעֵינָךְ עַל דִינָא בָּתַר סַגִיאֵי שְׁלַם דִינָא:
e: Do not follow the majority to do evil.
Do not respond with your opinion in a dispute [merely] to lean [toward one side] [(Do not) refrain from teaching what is proper in your eyes regarding a judgment]. It must be decided by the majority.
Do not show favor [even] to the poor in his dispute [judgment].

h: כִּ֣י תִפְגַּ֞ע שׁ֧וֹר אֹֽיִבְךָ֛ א֥וֹ חֲמֹר֖וֹ תֹּעֶ֑ה
t: אֲרֵי תִפְגַע תּוֹרָא דְסָנְאָךְ אוֹ חֲמָרֵהּ דְטָעֵי
e: If you come across your enemy’s ox or his donkey going astray,
bring it back to him.

h: כִּֽי־תִרְאֶ֞ה חֲמ֣וֹר שֹׂנַאֲךָ֗ רֹבֵץ֙ תַּ֣חַת מַשָּׂא֔וֹ
t: אֲרֵי תֶחֱזֵי חֲמָרָא דְסָנְאָךְ רְבִיעַ תְּחוֹת טוֹעֲנֵיהּ
מִשְׁבַּק תִּשְׁבּוֹק מָא דִבְלִבָּךְ עֲלוֹהִי וּתְפָרֵק עִמֵהּ:
e: If you see the donkey of your enemy lying under its burden,
and you might not want to help him [stop yourself from abandoning him],
[but you should] [[you should]] make every effort to help him [abandon what is in you heart against him and unload with him] .
Do not bend justice [even] for your needy in his dispute.

t: וְדִזְכֵי וְדִי נְפַק (דְכֵי) מִן דִינָא לָא תִקְטוֹל
e: Keep far away from anything false.
Do not kill an [one who is] innocent [or one who goes out innocent from judgment] righteous man,
for I will not acquit a wicked person.
Do not accept bribery,
for bribery blinds the clear-sighted [eyes of the wise],
and perverts the words of justice.
Do not oppress a stranger.
You [should] know the soul [feelings] of the stranger,
for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.
You may sow your land for six years,
and gather its crops.

h: וְהַשְּׁבִיעִ֞ת תִּשְׁמְטֶ֣נָּה וּנְטַשְׁתָּ֗הּ וְאָֽכְלוּ֙ אֶבְיֹנֵ֣י עַמֶּ֔ךָ
t: וּשְׁבִעֵתָא תַּשְׁמְטִנַהּ וְתַרְטְשִׁנַהּ וְיֵיכְלוּן מִסְכְּנֵי עַמָךְ
e: But on the seventh [year] you must let it rest, and abandon it [by not eating its produce], and let the needy among your people eat it.
What they leave over, the beasts of the field can eat.
Do the same with your vineyard and your olive [trees].
You may do your work six days,
but on the seventh day you must cease;
so that your ox and your donkey may rest,
and the son of your female slave may be refreshed, and [also] the stranger.
Preserve everything that I have said to you.
Do not mention the name of other [false] gods [of the peoples].
You must not cause it to be heard through your mouth.
Three times a year
you are to celebrate with [before] Me.

h: שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִים֩ תֹּאכַ֨ל מַצּ֜וֹת כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֗ךָ לְמוֹעֵד֙ חֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽאָבִ֔יב
t: שִׁבְעָא יוֹמִין תֵּיכוּל פַּטִירָא כְּמָא דִפַקֵידִתָּךְ לִזְמַן יַרְחָא דַאֲבִיבָא
e: You must keep the festival of Matzos.
You must eat matzos for seven days, as I have commanded you. [This festival must be celebrated] at the appointed time, during the month when the grain is ripened,
for in it [at this time] you went out of Egypt.
Do not appear before My Presence [Me] empty-handed.
[You must also keep] the Festival of Harvest, [with bringing bikurim] the first fruits of your labor,
which you planted in the field;
[also] the Festival of Ingathering, at the close of the year,
when you gather in [the fruits of] your labor from the field.
Three times a year,
every male among you must appear
before the Presence of the Master [of the world], Adonoy.

t: לָא תִכּוֹס עַל חֲמִיעַ דַם פִּסְחִי
וְלָא יְבִיתוּן בַּר מִן מַדְבְּחָא תַּרְבֵּי נִכְסַת חַגָא עַד צַפְרָא:
e: You must not sacrifice — while chometz is present — My [Pesach] sacrifice.
You must not allow to remain overnight [off the Altar] — the fat[s] of My [the] festival-offering — until morning.
The beginning of the first fruits of your land
must be brought to the House of [the Sanctuary of] Adonoy, your God.
You must not cook a young animal in the milk of its mother [eat meat with milk].
Behold, I will send an angel before you,
to guard you on the way,
and to bring you to the place that I have prepared.

h: הִשָּׁ֧מֶר מִפָּנָ֛יו וּשְׁמַ֥ע בְּקֹל֖וֹ אַל־תַּמֵּ֣ר בּ֑וֹ
t: אִסְתַּמַּר מִן קֳדָמוֹהִי וְקַבֵּל לְמֵימְרֵהּ לָא תְסָרֵב לְקִבְלֵהּ
e: Be careful in his presence and heed [obey] his voice [word]. Do not rebel against him;
for he cannot bear [pardon] your transgression,
as [in] My Name is in him [his word].
But if you truly listen to [obey] his voice [word],
and do all that I speak,
then I will be an enemy to your enemies,
and attack those who attack you.
My messenger will go before you,
and will bring you into [the land of] the Emorites, the Chittites,
the Perizzites, the Canaanites,
Chivites, and the Yevusites,
and I will then annihilate them.
You must not prostrate yourself to their [false] gods, nor serve [sacrifice to] them.
You must not adopt their customs.
You must totally destroy [their idols]
and completely break down their monuments.
You must serve [before] Adonoy, your God,
and He will bless your bread [food] and your water [drink].
I will eliminate [bad] sickness from your midst.
No woman will suffer miscarriage or remain childless in your land.
I will cause the number of your days to be full.

t: וְאֶמְסַר יָת כָּל בַּעֲלֵי דְבָבָךְ קֳדָמָךְ מְחַזְרֵי קְדָל:
e: I will send My dread ahead of you,
and I will bring panic to all the people
among whom you will come [to fight against].
I will make all your enemies turn their backs to [before] you.

t: וּתְתָרֵךְ יָת חִוָאֵי יָת כְּנַעֲנָאֵי וְיָת חִתָּאֵי מִן קֳדָמָךְ:
e: I will send [deadly] hornets ahead of you,
and they will drive out the Chivites, the Canaanites, and the Chittites from before you.

t: לָא אֱתָרֵכִנוּן מִן קֳדָמָךְ בְּשַׁתָּא חֲדָא
e: I will not drive them out in a single year,
lest the land become desolate,
and the beasts of the field multiply against you.
Little by little I will drive them from before you,
until you have increased
and occupy the land.

h: כִּ֣י אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּיֶדְכֶ֗ם אֵ֚ת יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ
t: וֶאֱשַׁוֵי יָת תְּחוּמָךְ מִיַמָא דְסוּף וְעַד יַמָא דִפְלִשְׁתָּאֵי
אֲרֵי אֶמְסַר בִּידֵיכוֹן יָת יָתְבֵי אַרְעָא
e: I will set your borders from the Reed Sea to the Philistine Sea,
and from the desert to the [Euphrates] river,
for I will deliver into your hands all the inhabitants of the land,
and you will drive them away before you.
Do not make a pact with them or with their [false] gods.
Do not allow them to live in your land,
since they may cause you to sin to [before] Me;
that you [might] worship their [false] gods,
and this would be a [fatal] trap to you.

h: וְאֶל־מֹשֶׁ֨ה אָמַ֜ר עֲלֵ֣ה אֶל־יְהוָ֗ה אַתָּה֙ וְאַהֲרֹן֙ נָדָ֣ב וַאֲבִיה֔וּא
t: וּלְמשֶׁה אֲמַר סַק לִקֳדָם יְיָ אַתְּ וְאַהֲרֹן נָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא
e: He [God] had said to Moshe, ‘Go up to [the Presence of] [before] Adonoy, you, Aharon, Nadav, Avihu,
and seventy of the elders of [the B’nei] Yisrael,
and prostrate yourselves at a distance.
Moshe alone shall approach [the Presence of] [before] Adonoy,
but they must not approach,
and the people must not go up with him.”

h: וַיָּבֹ֣א מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיְסַפֵּ֤ר לָעָם֙ אֵ֚ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה
t: וַאֲתָא משֶׁה וְאִשְׁתָּעִי לְעַמָא יָת כָּל פִּתְגָמַיָא דַיְיָ
וַאֲתֵיב כָּל עַמָא קָלָא חַד וַאֲמָרוּ
כָּל פִּתְגָמַיָא דִי מַלִיל יְיָ נַעְבֵּד:
e: Moshe came and told the people all the words of Adonoy,
and all the laws.
The people responded with one voice and said,
“All the words that Adonoy has spoken, we will do.”

t: וּכְתַב משֶׁה יָת כָּל פִּתְגָמַיָא דַיְיָ
e: Moshe wrote down all the words of Adonoy.
He arose early in the morning,
and built an altar beneath [at the foot of] the mountain,
and [also] twelve monuments [pillars]
for the twelve tribes of [the B’nei] Yisrael.
He sent the youths [first-born] of B’nei Yisrael
and they offered burnt-offerings,
and sacrificed oxen as peace-offerings to [before] Adonoy.
Moshe took half the blood
and put it in the basins,
and [the other] half the blood
he sprinkled on the altar.

h: וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה נַעֲשֶׂ֥ה וְנִשְׁמָֽע׃
t: וַאֲמָרוּ כֹּל דִי מַלִיל יְיָ נַעְבֵּד וּנְקַבֵּל:
e: He then took the Book of the Covenant,
and read it in the ears of [before] the people.
They said, “All that Adonoy has spoken, we will do and we will listen [obey].”

h: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֤ה דַֽם־הַבְּרִית֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר כָּרַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם
t: וַאֲמַר הָא דֵין דָם קְיָמָא דִגְזַר יְיָ עִמְכוֹן
e: Moshe then took the blood
and cast it on the [Altar to atone on behalf of the] people,
and he said, “Behold, this is the blood of the covenant which Adonoy has made with you
regarding all these words.”
Moshe and Aharon then went up
along with Nadav and Avihu,
and seventy of the elders of [the B’nei] Yisrael.
They saw [a vision of] the [Glory of the] God of Yisrael,
and under His feet [the throne of His Glory] [there was something] like a brickwork of sapphire [precious stone],
and it was like the essence [image] of heaven in purity.

t: וַהֲווֹ חָדָן בְּקָרְבָּנֵיהוֹן דְאִתְקַבָּלוּ בְּרַעֲוָא כְּאִלוּ אָכְלִין וְשָׁתָן:
e: But against the nobility of the B’nei Yisrael,
He [God] did not send His hand [there was no damage].
They envisioned [saw the Glory of] God,
and they [rejoiced in their sacrifices which were accepted graciously as if they] ate and drank.

h: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲלֵ֥ה אֵלַ֛י הָהָ֖רָה וֶהְיֵה־שָׁ֑ם
וְאֶתְּנָ֨ה לְךָ֜ אֶת־לֻחֹ֣ת הָאֶ֗בֶן וְהַתּוֹרָה֙ וְהַמִּצְוָ֔ה
t: וַאֲמַר יְיָ לְמשֶׁה סַק לִקֳדָמַי לְטוּרָא וֶהֱוֵי תַמָן
וְאֶתֵּן לָךְ יָת לוּחֵי אַבְנָא וְאוֹרַיְתָא וְתַפְקֶדְתָּא
e: Adonoy then said to Moshe, “Come up to [before] Me to the mountain and remain there.
I will give you the tablets of stone, the Torah and the commandment,
which I have written [in order] to teach them.”

t: וּסְלֵיק משֶׁה לְטוּרָא דְאִתְגְלִי עֲלוֹהִי יְקָרָא דַיְיָ:
e: Moshe and Yehoshua, his attendant, set out,
but [only] Moshe went up to the mountain [upon which the Glory] of God [was revealed].
He [Moshe] said to the elders, “Wait here for us
until we return to you,
and Aharon and Chur will be with you.
Whoever has a claim can approach [before] them.”
Moshe went up to the mountain,
and the cloud covered the mountain.

h: וַיִּקְרָ֧א אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֛ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י מִתּ֥וֹךְ הֶעָנָֽן׃
t: וּשְׁרָא יְקָרָא דַיְיָ עַל טוּרָא דְסִינַי
וּקְרָא לְמשֶׁה בְּיוֹמָא שְׁבִיעָאָה מִגוֹ עֲנָנָא:
e: The glory of Adonoy rested on Mount Sinai,
and the cloud covered it for six days.
On the seventh day, He called to Moshe from the midst of the cloud.
The appearance of Adonoy’s glory was like
[the appearance of] a consuming flame at the top to the mountain;
before the eyes of the B’nei Yisrael.

h: וַיָּבֹ֥א מֹשֶׁ֛ה בְּת֥וֹךְ הֶעָנָ֖ן וַיַּ֣עַל אֶל־הָהָ֑ר
t: וְעַל משֶׁה בְּגוֹ עֲנָנָא וּסְלֵיק לְטוּרָא
e: And Moshe came into the midst of the cloud. and went up into the mountain.
Moshe remained on the mountain
for forty days
and forty nights.
